claims.text: Road class: the print draws one connected chain of black round dots (about 2-2.5 atlas px across, pitch about 4 atlas px) with no colour and no casing. In band it has four runs: west edge to Sokundo, 18 dots from 1403.6,1452.3 to 1471.8,1450.8 passing over the river mouth at about 1438,1461; Sokundo to Kanae, 15 dots; Kanae to Rhup, 14 resolved dots plus about 2-3 absorbed into the R of the PESHUNOR lettering at 1529,1521; and a 2-dot stub leaving Rhup east, at 1573.2,1541.0 and 1575.0,1544.6. That is about 49 resolved dots, about 200 atlas px of major road. No dotted road reaches Aldorus or Sardil. Canon key: dotted = major roadways.

claims.text: River class: exactly one river, a thin solid-black unnamed line of a single weight, about 150 atlas px long (hand-traced polyline, +-10 px). claims.text: wiki-places.json (51 pages) carries no coordinates, so nothing in it can be placed inside the band by itself. By content search: Sokundo, Kanae, Aldorus (with or without macron) and Rhup occur in 0 pages; Sardil occurs once, in Leponnia (Leponnia Tanrin runs from the lands about Tamaron up to Sardil); Peshunor, Lamor, Aura and Hanath occur in Leponnia, with Peshunor and Lamor also in Epeshu; Dranimos is listed in the Leponnia Regions line. Only the Leponnia page is band-relevant.

gaps: The sea-lettering glyph R at x about 1570-1597 (clipped by the east edge) and the E at about 1670,1440 belong to a sea name that is not identified: the Great Chasmous Sea marker is far east at 1940.8,1505.4 and no marker sits near the letters.
Dranimos first letters and the Leponnia letters outside the band were not read in this band, so the full lettering paths (and whether the Leponnia marker anchors the lettering) are not established.
Exact river and coast lengths are hand-traced (+-10 px), and the count of road dots absorbed into the R glyph (about 2-3) is an estimate; per-dot positions of the road were not fitted to a spline.
The sea/land split (33.9%) and per-hex ink counts use colour and luminance thresholds on JPEG tiles (halos around labels count as paper), so they are estimates, not measured polygon areas.
Whether the plate-one density maps to this band at any scale is not derivable here (q01 gap: plate-one ground extent is unstated), so no names-per-hex target is set.
Relief for this band comes only from EPESHU_HF (not read in this question); the print carries no height, so any ridge name or height here must come from the DEM bake or be invented.
summary: Band M's print draws only a black coastline, a flat grey-olive sea with one island, one thin unnamed river, one dotted road chain (about 49 dots, Sokundo-Kanae-Rhup, none reaching Aldorus or Sardil), five identical single-ring settlements, and spaced region lettering; of 13 plate-one classes 9 are missing outright (peaks and heights, relief texture, washes, shields, secondary road, trails, braid, forks, knot) and 4 appear in another dress. The data matches the print only for the five city-anchors, with 1 marker (Leponnia), 1 straight-chord Sun Road trace, 1 sea lane, 0 traced roads and no placeable wiki page, and 7 of the 45 whole hexes are bare land.
